findings: l.1990–2004: lem:spread_top is false as printed. Counterexample (formal, GX.cex_spread_top_halfCut / GX.not_spreadTopPrinted): M = N = ℂ, S = ∅, q = id, p: M̃^∅ → ℂ the universal covering, R = {Im ≠ 0}, T = the topology of ℂ generated by the usual one and {Im ≥ 0}. All hypotheses hold; p⁻¹{Im ≥ 0} and p⁻¹{Im < 0} are p^*T-open, so p^*T is disconnected and (a), (e) fail. The proof uses 'N strongly connected' (l.2018) and 'R̂ weakly connected' (l.2047), neither of which is a hypothesis.

l.2047: 'R̂ is weakly connected' does not follow even when T is connected (informal, not formalized; the formal correction only needs the half-cut counterexample): M = N = ℂ*, S = ∅, p the universal covering (log), T cutting ℂ* along the positive real ray with the ray glued to the upper bank; p^*T splits M̃ into strips. Corrected form: assume p⁻¹(R) connected (true when R is portly for the natural topology, as in the application l.2096).

l.2029/2034: the Claim's 'We may assume that Ô ∩ R̂ is connected' is unproved (the argument lifts a path from x̂ to some point over z, not to ẑ) and is exactly (c): GX.isPortly_strongPullTop_iff_local. It fails (FORMAL, GX.cex_spread_top_sector, GX.not_spreadTopConnCE): M = N = ℂ, S = {0}, M̃^{0} ≅ 𝔻_∞ the logarithmic covering completed at 0 (GX.exists_homeomorph_maxBranched_qDisc), q = id, R = ℂ∖{0} (portly for both topologies, p⁻¹R connected), T = usual ⊓ generateFrom{{0} ∪ {Re > 0}} (first countable, LPC, agreeing with the usual topology on R). The preimage of the sector is p^*T-open and p^*T-connected through the branch point, its regular part p⁻¹{Re > 0} is not connected: (c), (e) and the Claim's local hypothesis all fail. theo:local_virt_tame uses (c)/(e) through (D) and the strong branched covering; its proof inherits the gap.

l.2025: 'M̃^S → M is Galoisian and thus so is M̃^S → N' is asserted without argument; it is true (GX.isGaloisian_of_comp: deck transitivity over q⁻¹(M∖S) by uniqueness of lifts, dense orbits, discrete fibres from M∖S slsc in M), using N Hausdorff, LPC, first countable and M∖S ⊆ ord_q (GX.compl_subset_ordY_of_comp).

l.2017–2018 'lem:path_covering' is applied relative to an open connected O (GX.exists_path_of_isPortly_of_isOpen), and the Claim's second part needs fibres of p discrete (from M∖S slsc in M) to pick Ô ∩ p⁻¹(y) = {ŷ}.

Proof BUILT (WP-35g) for all five clauses: GX.spread_top_of_local proves (a) first countable+connected+LPC, (b), (c), (d), (e) exactly as printed under three added hypotheses (N → M Galoisian; p⁻¹(R) connected; StrongLocallyConnectedOrd). Both topological added hypotheses are now shown necessary in the presence of all the others (in both counterexamples q = id is Galoisian): the half-cut example satisfies the local hypothesis (GX.strongLocallyConnectedOrd_halfCut, via GX.exists_homeomorph_maxBranched_empty: M̃^∅ → ℂ is a homeomorphism) and p^*T is disconnected; the sector example satisfies p⁻¹R connected and (c), (e) fail.

(d) without 'N → M Galoisian' is not formalized either way. Informal counterexample sketch: N a non-normal finite intermediate covering of a space with non-abelian π₁ (e.g. ℂ minus two points, S = ∅) has Γ(N/M) trivial, so any T is allowed; take T cut (as in halfCutTop) at one point n₀ of a fibre and natural elsewhere; a deck transformation γ of M̃ sending a point over n₁ ≠ n₀ to a point over n₀ (exists, M̃ → M Galoisian) is not p^*T-continuous there.
The dispatch cites the proof as l.2068–2136; that range is the proof of theo:local_virt_tame. The proof of lem:spread_top is l.2010–2061 (it follows rem:intuitively_spread_thinner_than).

labels.label: rem:intuitively_spread_thinner_than

hypotheses.paper: p a spread, T thinner than T_N
hypotheses.note: the coarsest-bound half needs neither: every locally connected σ' finer than T_M with p σ'→T continuous is finer than p^*T

RULED (DEC-87(d)): read 'in the setting of lem:spread_top' — every hypothesis of GX.spread_top_of_local (DEC-80(c) form); 'coarsest topology making p a spread' = IsGreatest among σ' ≤ T_{M̃^S} (finer than the natural topology, mathlib order) with p : (M̃^S, σ') → (N, T) a spread

findings: l.2006: read literally, 'p^*T is the coarsest topology on M such that (M,p^*T) → (N,T) is a spread' is false in general — p^*T need not be a spread (GX.not_isSpread_strongPullTop_ratTop: p = id on ℝ, T generated by the usual topology and ℚ), and the comparison must be restricted to topologies finer than T_M (GX.not_isGreatest_strongPullTop_unrestricted: p : ℝ → point, the indiscrete topology also makes p a spread).

WP-40d: in the lemma the remark accompanies the intuition HOLDS: under lem:spread_top's hypotheses in the ruled form (DEC-80(c)), p^*T is the coarsest spread topology finer than that of M̃^S (GX.intuitively_spread_thinner_of_local, from (e)). In general: every spread topology finer than T_M is finer than p^*T (GX.le_strongPullTop_of_isSpread), and p^*T is the coarsest one exactly when it is locally connected (GX.isSpread_strongPullTop_iff, GX.isGreatest_strongPullTop). The 'However' sentence is GX.cex_component_not_strongPull_connected (ℝ cut at 0).

labels.label: def:topological_spaces_continuous_map

hypotheses.note: the definition needs no continuity of p; the API lemmas carry IsSpread p where used

findings: WP-41q: DEC-87(e) certifies the row in GXScaffold.SingularII.Models; this module keeps the unmarked API and the verbatim-wording identity GX.strongPullTop_eq_generateFrom_union (status 'closed' here refers to that identity; the label's attribution is Models').

kb_proposals: A local `set T := (some topology)` (or any local hypothesis of type TopologicalSpace E) is a LOCAL INSTANCE and makes every later term that synthesizes an instance on E (Homeomorph coercions, .symm, .toEquiv, deck_apply's instance args, deckGroup) pick it: use a @[reducible] def for the second topology (GX.pullTamTop) and factor statements about the natural topology into T-free lemmas (GX.base_preimage_image_galoisian).

Binder order: a hypothesis about the NATURAL topology (Continuous Pj, IsBranchedCovering Pj) must come BEFORE a binder {T : TopologicalSpace E}, or be written with weakTopMax explicitly; otherwise it silently refers to T.
deck_apply (GX.Branched.Galois) takes p EXPLICIT: deck_apply _ hφ x; under a local second topology use congrFun hφ x instead (membership in deckGroup is p ∘ φ = p by definition).

The spinless massive particle 𝔼^{1,2}_α (α > 0, α ≠ 2π) is ready as a singular (Isom₀, 𝔼^{1,2})-model: GX.MassCyl, GX.IsMassiveStructure, GX.exists_isMassiveStructure, sing = axis (GX.massCyl_sing), tame (GX.massCyl_isTame), Ẽ_α ≅ 𝔻_∞ × ℝ over it (GX.massCyl_exists_homeomorph), Γ(Ẽ_α/E_α) = Γ_α (GX.exists_gamma_eq_of_over), time translations in Aut (GX.massCyl_timeShift_mem_aeAut).

For §4 (prop:BTZ_virt_tame, WP-28): the BTZ tamifying topology T of sec:mot_BTZ is GX.btzGenTop = GX.hornTop on 𝔻_∞ × ℝ, with first countability, local path-connectedness, Γ_α-continuity, (A) for Γ_α\(𝔻_∞ × ℝ) and (D) already proved for hornTop (tamTop univ); what remains for BTZ is (B): btzDev's hornTop-continuity at the axis.
Sing of a cylinder quotient when the holonomy generator has finite order (α ∈ 2πℤ, α ≥ 4π): GX.apex_notMem_support_of_sep — the developing map identifies two points of different orbits near the apex.

IsTamifyingTopology transports along a homeomorphism Φ : M̃ ≃ₜ Y over M: induced Φ T' with (A) from coinduced_compose + GX.coinduced_induced_of_surjective, LPC via IsOpenEmbedding.locPathConnectedSpace, first countability via firstCountableTopology_induced, (D) via IsPortly.image_of_isOpenMap on Φ.symm (GX.massCyl_isTamifying_tamTop).
